lucas: heads up — noticed ~12% p50->p95 tail jump on host preparse after yesterday's kernel-selector roll. pprof attached :eyes:
maya: can you paste the top stacks? do we know if it's tokenization or grpc framing?
lucas: early read shows spend in `parse_token_stream` and `header_unfold`. quick top:
```
50.2%  parse_token_stream
18.7%  header_unfold
9.1%   kv_cache_lookup
6.0%   http2_frame_decode
```
anya: kv metrics spiking on evictions, TTL looks low during the burst — think the new batching heuristic increases concurrency and thrashes hot KV shards
sam: interesting — kernel selector change bumped up minibatch size for small requests. that could keep more context in flight -> more KV pressure
lucas: repro curl to hit slow path: `curl -N -H 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' https://canary.rw-infer.internal/v1/stream` — streaming microbursts show smallwrites pattern and repeated `header_unfold`
maya: can we snapshot perf and verify on canary only? if it's KV thrash we should tune cache TTL + shard affinity
sam: propose revert kernel drop on canary and land a microfix: reduce minibatch for <=64 tokens, add KV pinning for those streams
lucas: ok rolling canary revert now (infra-bot triggered)
infra-bot: deploy started: revert-kernel-selector-pr-4523 to canary (id: dpl_8892)
anya: will monitor kv.evictions, host.preparse.tail_latency, and http2.writev_count
lucas: adding INF-2398 to track root cause + validate batching heuristics
maya: also add a small pprof + flame job and mark as blocker for next kernel rollout
sam: +1
lucas: thanks — followup in INF-2398, posting flame links in the ticket :link:
